With Ray Middleton and Allan Callow backing up, Bels took the team and there was also some good walking by the Johns Dunsford and Hall, who came in together with Dave McMullen not far behind.
In the 20 kilo's they were led home by John Hall, well behind Shaun Lightman, and John Dunsford despite his 50 kilo's a week earlier managed a commendable performance.
With the retirement of Allan Callow and Ray Hall, it was up to John Dunsford to be fourth man home. George Beecham was another to fall by the wayside.
Belgrave were 2nd team to Southend with Lawton, Ray Middleton and John Hall in the Bels. team. Our other walkers were John Dunsford, Dave McMullen, John Bromley and Ray Hall.

The battle between these two lasted up to the finishing line with John Dunsford getting the verdict (and a medal) by four seconds. Overall it was an excellent win for Belgrave and an excellent turn out although one place had to be refilled due to the non-appearance of one walker who had originally been selected.

John Dunsford had his days as did Dave McMullen, in between his complaints about his performances, despite his gold G.L.C. medal. Ray Hall began to regain his fitness but a stomach virus put paid to that.
Over at Wembley on the same day, John Dunsford finished 5th in the London Business Houses 7 miles championship in 58 minutes 35 seconds.
However, this position went to Stuart Bennett with the rest of the field strung out over a lap. John Dunsford was sweeper up.
Dave "I'll never break the hour again" McMullen only had 2 minutes 44 seconds to spare and Len Evans, Martin Bennett and John Dunsford also were under the hour.
With John Bromley in hospital and John Dunsford losing his qualification for this race, last year's team was sorely depleted and the resultant performance was below our normal standard.

John Dunsford was not quite as fit as he has been and could not catch McMullen over the closing stages. Paul Wiltshire put up a distinguished time and to quote one of the judges, "could be very good if he will get his arms right".
John Hall walked a rather sleepy sort of race and never got going but John Dunsford delighted in turning the tables on Dave McMullen again. Ray Hall, not too fit at the moment,was our 8th man.

First away in the Boy's 2 miles race was John Dunsford, who unfortunately was later disqualified with only 200m to go. The reason was that he overdid the early part and had to fight over the second half.

Further back, John Hall walked quite a good one in the hot conditions to beat Southend's Banyard and Rosser whilst Dave McMullen came under the judges ban as did many other men. John Dunsford was at one time seen walking backwards! Gerry Cameron, after a long trip down from Dunfermline, held off Ray Hall.
We only had three starters and so had no team chance. John Hall walked a steady race to finish 5th with Paul Wiltshire and John Dunsford backing up.

On the same evening that John Dunsford was at West London Stadium, competing in the Middlesex 10 km Championship, Mrs. Dunsford took son Jonathon over to the Essex Championships to compete in a boys race (which he won) and ended up competing in a women's 1 mile race.
John Hall placed 31st with John Dunsford and Dave McMullen well up. Ray Hall was forced to retire but Bob Picton and John Keown completed the distance.

By 17 miles Carl had got back up to 4th with Len Duquemin 5th, however, at this point he tired drastically and recorded 24 minutes for the last 2 miles to finish 11th. John Dunsford was our fifth man with John Bromley and Bob Picton walking the last few miles together.
The tenacity of Dave McMullen, D.Hall and John Dunsford showed this spirit and the pity was that E.Stroud could not be included in the team and rewarded for his fine walk.
Next away was the Senior mens 15 km with John Dunsford finishing 23rd. Higher up the field Carl Lawton finished 3rd to Bob Dobson with John Bromley almost catching International John Webb.
Carl got going again to hold off Hodkinson and Michel (Surrey). Further back John Dunsford walked well for 10th with John Keown and Dave King well down but finishing.
An expedition of three Belgrave Vets ( John Bromley, John Dunsford and Dave McMullen) set forth on the last week-end of September to contest a walk in Hamburg.

Middleton and Moullin walked steadily through pulling back places over the undulating course, and John Hall ambled through as 4th man. John Dunsford managed to overcome the usual consistency of John Bromley who was suffering from stomach ache.

John Moullin, John Dunsford and Dave King who made up our scoring team deserve praise but to win the 'Blue Riband', the oldest of the Road Walking Championships requires an utter dedication to training and team work.
Three of our walkers are hoping to go to Toronto, Canada in August to compete in some veteran events, so good luck to DAVE McMULLEN, JOHN BROMLEY and JOHN DUNSFORD.
